title: Shop for cheaper home and car insurance with an agent
summary: A user had Claude pull their policy from email, compare rates and phone insurers with a calling tool they built; they report saving about $2,500 a year.
agent_role: Read the current policy from email, checked competing rates and placed calls to insurance agencies; the human built the calling tool and chose the bundle.
outcome: Author reports saving about $2,500 per year on a home and auto bundle.
what_they_did: The poster asked Claude to find their insurance policy in email and check competing rates. Claude could not call insurers, so they built a phone calling tool for it. The agent then contacted agencies for quotes.
how_it_went: The author says the agent found a home and auto bundle saving about $2,500 a year. They have open-sourced the calling tool.
worth_knowing: The main barrier was that insurers wanted phone calls; without a calling tool the agent could only compare rates online.
prompt: Find my current home and car insurance policies in my email and summarize the coverage, limits, deductibles and yearly cost. Then look up competing quotes from insurers in [your state or city] for the same coverage, including bundles. Put the options in a table with price and any coverage differences. If you can make calls, write a short call script first and show it to me before calling anyone. Do not switch, cancel or buy any policy; give me your recommendation and wait for my decision.

curation.rationale: A useful everyday finance task where the agent read a policy from email, compared rates and phoned insurers, with a concrete savings claim; details are thin and partly promote the author's own tool.
